environment.protocol: one fixed 896px noise image, 20 distinct questions per config; fresh server process for apc_off vs apc_on; warmup excluded

findings: KV prefix caching gives 8.9x warm speedup (969 -> 109 ms) but ONLY when the image precedes the changing question in the prompt.
With the question first, caching-on warm TTFT (351 ms) matches caching-off (335 ms): the changing prefix makes KV reuse impossible.

Unexpected: even with --no-enable-prefix-caching, warm requests drop 943 -> 335 ms. vLLM's multimodal preprocessor/encoder cache is a separate layer that still dedupes the identical image, skipping vision encoding while the full LLM prefill is re-paid.
Warm apc_off TTFT (335 ms) matches EXP-T text prefill at ~1049 tokens (302 ms): consistent with encoding skipped, prefill paid.
